batchName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284) - Medium Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284)

questions.question: In 193, legions in which frontier province proclaimed Septimius Severus emperor?
questions.explanation: His legions in Noricum, roughly modern Austria, hailed him emperor in 193, the Year of the Five Emperors. Four years of civil war followed.
questions.sourceQuote: In 193 his legions in Noricum, a frontier province roughly in modern Austria, proclaimed him emperor.

questions.question: To which social class did Septimius Severus's family belong?
questions.explanation: His family was equestrian, the propertied class just below senators. They had Libyan, Punic and Italian roots.
questions.sourceQuote: His family belonged to the equestrian order, the propertied class just below senators, and had Libyan, Punic and Italian roots.

questions.question: In what capacity did Zenobia first take power in Palmyra in 267?
options: As regent for her ten-year-old son
As a governor appointed by Rome
As a general elected by the army
As high priestess of Palmyra's gods
As queen by right of her own birth
questions.explanation: After her husband was assassinated in 267, Zenobia, then in her late twenties, ruled as regent for their young son. Her court was known for philosophers and religious tolerance.
questions.sourceQuote: When he was assassinated in 267, his widow Zenobia, then in her late twenties, took power as regent for their ten-year-old son.

questions.question: What role did Aurelian play at the battle of Naissus before becoming emperor?
questions.explanation: Aurelian was the cavalry commander at Naissus, where a Gothic invasion was crushed in 268 or 269. He took the throne in 270.
questions.sourceQuote: His cavalry commander there, Aurelian, took the throne in 270.

questions.question: How do modern historians view ancient tales that Elagabalus was depraved and bloodthirsty?
options: As drawn from his own memoirs
questions.explanation: Modern historians think most of the lurid stories about him are invented. What coins and inscriptions do confirm is his religious change of 220 and his marriage to a Vestal Virgin.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancient writers called him depraved and bloodthirsty, but modern historians think most such tales are invented.

questions.question: Where was Caracalla's younger brother killed on his orders in 211?
questions.explanation: Caracalla had his brother, Geta, killed in their mother's apartments, and the young man died clinging to Julia Domna. Caracalla then bought the army's goodwill with pay rises.
questions.sourceQuote: Soon after their father died in 211, Caracalla had his brother, Geta, killed in their mother's apartments; the young man died clinging to Julia Domna.

questions.question: Caracalla's obsession with Alexander the Great led him to do what?
options: Found a new city named after himself
Adopt the Greek language at court
Form a phalanx of spearmen in Macedonian style
questions.explanation: Caracalla formed a phalanx, a block of spearmen in the old Macedonian style. He also executed people who mocked him.
questions.sourceQuote: Obsessed with the Macedonian conqueror Alexander, he formed a phalanx, a block of spearmen in the old Macedonian style, and executed people who mocked him.

questions.question: Why is the Historia Augusta an unreliable source for this period?
options: It survives only as a short list of names
questions.explanation: The Historia Augusta, a late Roman collection of imperial biographies, invented events and letters. It also reshaped Zenobia to flatter whichever emperor it praised.
questions.sourceQuote: The Historia Augusta, a late Roman collection of imperial biographies, invented events and letters, and reshaped Zenobia to suit whichever emperor it praised.

questions.question: At which places did Aurelian defeat Zenobia's army in 272? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Aurelian won at Immae, about 40 km from Antioch, and then near Emesa (Homs). At Emesa her 70,000 men nearly won before breaking ranks.
questions.sourceQuote: He beat her army at Immae, about 40 km (25 miles) from Antioch, then near Emesa, modern Homs, where her 70,000 men nearly won before breaking ranks.

questions.question: Why could so many generals seize the throne during the Crisis of the Third Century?
options: Emperors were chosen by lot each year
Rome had never fixed rules of succession
The Praetorian Guard elected every ruler
questions.explanation: With no fixed succession rules, any general with a big army could try his luck. Over 50 men claimed the imperial title.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome had never fixed rules of succession, so any general with a big army could try his luck.
